issues.body: When PyYAML is absent and CI is truthy, `_SEAM_MUST_RUN` is true, so the class is not skipped. `test_pyyaml_is_installed_in_ci` fails, but unittest does not stop the class; each later test calls `_job_hosting`, which executes `yaml.safe_load(...)` while `yaml` is `None`. The run therefore reports the intended failure plus multiple AttributeErrors, contrary to the stated one-clear-failure behavior. The added unit tests only test the predicate and decorator metadata under the current interpreter; they never execute the class in a CI-marked process where importing yaml fails.
issues.fix_hint: Fail once before the YAML-dependent tests execute, for example by making each dependent test/class skip after a dedicated CI dependency failure or by raising one clear setup-time failure without subsequently dereferencing `yaml`. Add a subprocess test that masks PyYAML, sets a CI marker, runs the relevant suite, and asserts a nonzero result with the clear dependency message and no `None.safe_load`/AttributeError cascade.
issues.title: Missing PyYAML in CI still produces cascading errors

verdict.summary: The local-only skip policy is sound, and the policy tests correctly pin common truthy/falsy CI markers. However, the CI-missing-PyYAML path does not behave as claimed: the new assertion fails, then unittest continues into every remaining seam test, where `yaml.safe_load` dereferences `None`. This recreates the noisy cascade the change says it prevents. The test suite also does not exercise that real missing-parser/CI execution path, so it cannot catch the discrepancy.
